description:
FILED s449s (Opus, agent S of round 7), found probing #563.  PRE-EXISTING;
#563's repair does not reach it (the `>` survives as an Operator there, so
the run is not derailed and PExpr's rebuild owns it).

REPRO (probed, perl 5.40.3; a directory holding a.t and b.t):

    my @f = sort <./gd/[ab].t>;
    perl: ./gd/a.t ./gd/b.t
    PCL : statement dropped -- "Handle single node of unknown type. Dump:"

    PPI: Word(sort) Operator(<) Operator(.) Regexp::Match(/gd/)
         Structure([) Word(ab) Structure(])
         Operator(.) Word(t) Operator(>) Structure(;)

CAUSE, located: `Pl::PExpr::_fix_ppi_glob_after_block` decides whether a
`<` ... `>` run is a glob by looking for a metacharacter, and it counts them
only in NON-Structure tokens:

    $has_glob_chars = 1 if ref($t) !~ /^PPI::Structure/ && $c =~ /[\*\?\[\]~]/;

The exclusion is itself deliberate and load-bearing (its comment: a
`PPI::Structure::Subscript` contains `[1]`, which would falsely match), so
the fix is NOT to drop it -- a bracket class in a glob is a Structure that
is not a subscript, and the two have to be told apart.  Note the run here
also carries a Regexp token (`/gd/`) whose content is part of the pattern,
which is the same §14 damage one notch milder.

Since the pattern has no other metacharacter the rebuild declines, the run
stays a comparison chain, and the statement is dropped.  With a `*` anywhere
in the same pattern (`<./gd/[ab]*.t>`) it rebuilds and works -- so the bug is
exactly "a bracket class is not counted as a metacharacter".

BAR: the class spelling with and without a second metacharacter, vs perl;
the `[1]` subscript case the exclusion exists for (`my @x=(1,2); print
$x[1];` and `$r->[1]`) unchanged; corpus-diff; a row beside the #563 rows in
`Pl/t/readline-ternary-01.t` or in `Pl/t/glob-01.t`.
subject: A diamond glob whose only metacharacter is a BRACKET CLASS drops: `<./gd/[ab].t>` -- _fix_ppi_glob_after_block counts metacharacters in TOKENS only, and PPI made the class a Structure
